canonical.name: The current library had no general normed-space dual definition on an earlier page: only the algebraic dual and the concrete L^p duality package were already on disk, so the basic dual-space definition is built here before any norming or separation corollary.

The chain-union upper-bound step is split out as its own lemma instead of being buried inside the Zorn proof, because later authoring needs that step as a named dependency and not as an unnamed sentence inside the maximal-extension argument.

The design keeps both the direct norm-preserving extension theorem and a separate theorem stating that no closure hypothesis is needed. The second item is retained as an explicit scope guard so later authoring does not silently add a false closed-subspace hypothesis.

The choice-strength remark deliberately overlaps the earlier draft recorded-not-proved item rem-hahn-banach-choice-strength. The new page-local id is kept because FA-4 is where Hahn-Banach first becomes load-bearing, and the duplication is recorded rather than hidden.

The examples page starts by comparing the abstract norming-functional theorem with the already-scaffolded concrete L^p-L^q duality formula from MT-16, so the companion does not pretend that the abstract Hahn-Banach existence result is the first place the library can see a norming functional explicitly.

The codimension-one interval produced by the one-step extension lemma is kept visible on the examples page by computing one explicit nondegenerate interval rather than leaving the admissible-value phenomenon buried inside the proof of the A-page lemma.

Nonuniqueness is kept as its own B-page leaf rather than folded into the computed interval example, because later pages may need the phenomenon itself without replaying the coordinates of one concrete interval calculation.

The B-page open-questions remark is only a local signpost to the already-published open-question records about Hamel bases and discontinuous additive functions; it is not a second source bundle and is intentionally non-load-bearing.
